sentences.heading: Theory of Operation > Functional Description > Timeout Controls > Bus Timeout or Stretch Timeout
sentences.text: With the configuration of `TIMEOUT_CTRL.MODE`, one of two types of timeouts can be selected.

sentences.heading: Theory of Operation > Functional Description > Timeout Controls > Bus Timeout or Stretch Timeout
sentences.text: If a `STRETCH_TIMEOUT` is selected, the Controller Module detects when some other device holds SCL low for more cycles than than `TIMEOUT_CTRL.VAL` clock ticks.

sentences.heading: Theory of Operation > Functional Description > Timeout Controls > Bus Timeout or Stretch Timeout
sentences.text: If a bus timeout occurs while the Controller Module is active, the corresponding `CONTROLLER_EVENTS.BUS_TIMEOUT` bit is set, halting the Controller Module and requiring handling from software before the next command will process. <!-- TODO:

sentences.heading: Theory of Operation > Functional Description > Timeout Controls > Bus Timeout or Stretch Timeout
sentences.text: In addition, if the last command byte addressing the module issued a read operation, `TARGET_EVENTS.BUS_TIMEOUT` will be set, causing the Target Module to stretch the clock on read operations until software handles the event.

sentences.heading: Theory of Operation > Functional Description > Timeout Controls > SCL Idle Timeout
sentences.text: `HOST_TIMEOUT_CTRL` is optionally enabled, determined by whether the register value is nonzero.

sentences.heading: Theory of Operation > Functional Description > Timeout Controls > Target Module Stretch Timeout
sentences.text: If enabled with `TARGET_TIMEOUT_CTRL.EN`, the Target Module will automatically NACK transactions if it stretches the clock for more cycles than `TARGET_TIMEOUT_CTRL.VAL`.

sentences.heading: Theory of Operation > Functional Description > Interrupts > Controller Module
sentences.text: Firmware can configure the threshold value via the register `HOST_FIFO_CONFIG.RX_THRESH`.

sentences.heading: Theory of Operation > Functional Description > Interrupts > Controller Module
sentences.text: Firmware can configure the threshold value via the register `HOST_FIFO_CONFIG.FMT_THRESH`.

sentences.heading: Theory of Operation > Functional Description > Interrupts > Controller Module
sentences.text: If the module transmits a byte and the 9th bit is a NACK from the Target/Bus, the `controller_halt` interrupt is usually asserted (modulo the effect of `FDATA.NAKOK`).

sentences.heading: Theory of Operation > Functional Description > Interrupts > Controller Module
sentences.text: Though normal clock stretching does not count as SCL interference, if the module detects that a target device has held SCL low and stretched any given SCL cycle for more than `TIMEOUT_CTRL.VAL` clock ticks this will cause the stretch timeout interrupt to be asserted.

sentences.heading: Theory of Operation > Functional Description > Interrupts > Controller Module
sentences.text: This interrupt is suppressed, however, if `TIMEOUT_CTRL.EN` is deasserted low or if the bus timeout is selected for `TIMEOUT_CTRL.MODE`.

sentences.heading: Theory of Operation > Functional Description > Interrupts > Target Module
sentences.text: If software sets the bit `CTRL.TX_STRETCH_CTRL_EN`, the Target Module will require software to confirm release of the TX FIFO at the beginning of every read transfer addressed to it.

sentences.heading: Theory of Operation > Functional Description > Interrupts > Target Module
sentences.text: This behaviour may be useful to software, as any remaining data in the TX FIFO after a Sr/P condition may no longer apply to the next transfer, so it may have to be cleared out via `FIFO_CTRL.TXRST`.

sentences.heading: Theory of Operation > Functional Description > Interrupts > Target Module
sentences.text: Firmware can configure the threshold value via the register `TARGET_FIFO_CONFIG.ACQ_THRESH`.

sentences.heading: Theory of Operation > Functional Description > Interrupts > Target Module
sentences.text: Firmware can configure the threshold value via the register `TARGET_FIFO_CONFIG.TX_THRESH`.

sentences.heading: Theory of Operation > Functional Description > Interrupts > Target Module
sentences.text: If ACK Control Mode is enabled, check the relevant bits in `STATUS` to determine the reason(s).

sentences.heading: Theory of Operation > Functional Description > Interrupts > Target Module
sentences.text: Firmware can configure the timeout value via the register `HOST_TIMEOUT_CTRL`.

sentences.heading: Theory of Operation > Application Notes > Override Mode for Direct Pin Access
sentences.text: To enter override mode, the register field `OVRD.TXOVRDEN` is asserted by software.

sentences.heading: Theory of Operation > Application Notes > Override Mode for Direct Pin Access
sentences.text: In this state the output drivers `scl_tx_o` and `sda_tx_o` are controlled directly by the register fields `OVRD.SCLVAL` and `OVRD.SDAVAL`.

sentences.heading: Theory of Operation > Application Notes > Override Mode for Direct Pin Access
sentences.text: When `OVRD.SCLVAL` and `OVRD.SDAVAL` are set high, the virtual open drain configuration will leave the output resistively pulled high, and controllable by remote targets.

sentences.heading: Theory of Operation > Application Notes > Override Mode for Direct Pin Access
sentences.text: In this state, with SCL or SDA asserted high, the register fields `VAL.SCL_RX` and `VAL.SDA_RX` can be used to receive inputs (including remote acknowledgments) from target devices.

sentences.text: Input the integer timing parameters, THD_STA_MIN, TSU_STA_MIN, THD_DAT_MIN, TSU_DAT_MIN, T_BUF_MIN and T_STO_MIN into their corresponding registers (`TIMING2.THD_STA`, `TIMING2.TSU_STA`, `TIMING3.THD_DAT`, `TIMING3.TSU_DAT`, `TIMING4.T_BUF`, `TIMING4.T_STO`)

sentences.text: - The registers `TIMING0.THIGH` and `TIMING0.TLOW` will be taken care of in a later step.

sentences.heading: Programmer's Guide > Initialization > Timing Parameter Tuning Algorithm
sentences.text: `TIMING1.T_R` and `TIMING1.T_F`.

sentences.heading: Programmer's Guide > Initialization > Timing Parameter Tuning Algorithm
sentences.text: - It is, for instance, perfectly acceptable to simply set TLOW to the minimum possible value: $$ \textrm{TIMING0.TLOW}=\textrm{TLOW_MIN} $$

sentences.heading: Programmer's Guide > Initialization > Timing Parameter Tuning Algorithm
sentences.text: THIGH is then set to satisfy both constraints in the desired SCL period and in the minimum permissible values for t<sub>HIGH</sub>: $$ \textrm{TIMING0.THIGH}=\max(\textrm{PERIOD}-\textrm{T_R} - \textrm{TIMING0.TLOW} -\textrm{T_F}, \textrm{THIGH_MIN}) $$

sentences.heading: Programmer's Guide > Controller Module Operations > Writing `n` bytes to a device:
sentences.text: - `FDATA.START` = 1;

sentences.heading: Programmer's Guide > Controller Module Operations > Writing `n` bytes to a device:
sentences.text: - `FDATA.FBYTE` = < 7-bit address + write bit >.

sentences.heading: Programmer's Guide > Controller Module Operations > Writing `n` bytes to a device:
sentences.text: Fill the FMT FIFO by writing to `FDATA.FBYTE` `n`-1 times.

sentences.heading: Programmer's Guide > Controller Module Operations > Writing `n` bytes to a device:
sentences.text: - `FDATA.STOP` = 1;

sentences.heading: Programmer's Guide > Controller Module Operations > Writing `n` bytes to a device:
sentences.text: - `FDATA.FBYTE` = < last byte >.

sentences.heading: Programmer's Guide > Controller Module Operations > Writing `n` bytes to a device:
sentences.text: - If `INTR_STATE.CONTROLLER_HALT` is 1, the transaction failed.

sentences.heading: Programmer's Guide > Controller Module Operations > Writing `n` bytes to a device:
sentences.text: - Check `CONTROLLER_EVENTS` for the reason, reset the FMT FIFO with `FIFO_CTRL.FMTRST`, and clear the latched events.

sentences.heading: Programmer's Guide > Controller Module Operations > Writing `n` bytes to a device:
sentences.text: - Otherwise, if `INTR_STATE.CMD_COMPLETE` is 1 and `STATUS.FMTEMPTY` is 1, the transaction succeeded.

sentences.heading: Programmer's Guide > Controller Module Operations > Reading `n` bytes from a device:
sentences.text: - `FDATA.START` = 1;

sentences.heading: Programmer's Guide > Controller Module Operations > Reading `n` bytes from a device:
sentences.text: - `FDATA.FBYTE` = < 7-bit address + read bit >.

sentences.heading: Programmer's Guide > Controller Module Operations > Reading `n` bytes from a device:
sentences.text: - `FDATA.READB` = 1;

sentences.heading: Programmer's Guide > Controller Module Operations > Reading `n` bytes from a device:
sentences.text: - `FDATA.STOP` = 1;

sentences.heading: Programmer's Guide > Controller Module Operations > Reading `n` bytes from a device:
sentences.text: - `FDATA.FBYTE` = < `n` >.

sentences.heading: Programmer's Guide > Controller Module Operations > Reading `n` bytes from a device:
sentences.text: - If `STATUS.FMTEMPTY` bit is 1.

sentences.heading: Programmer's Guide > Controller Module Operations > Reading `n` bytes from a device:
sentences.text: - **Or** if `INTR_STATE.FMT_THRESHOLD` bit is 1 ( as long as `FIFO_CTRL.FMTILVL` is set to 1).

sentences.heading: Programmer's Guide > Controller Module Operations > Reading `n` bytes from a device:
sentences.text: - If `INTR_STATE.CONTROLLER_HALT` is 1.

sentences.heading: Programmer's Guide > Controller Module Operations > Reading `n` bytes from a device:
sentences.text: If the `INTR_STATE.CONTROLLER_HALT` bit is 1, then set `FIFO_CTRL.FMTRST` to reset the FMT FIFO, clear latched events in `CONTROLLER_EVENTS`, and go back to step 1.

sentences.heading: Programmer's Guide > Controller Module Operations > Reading `n` bytes from a device:
sentences.text: If `STATUS.FMTEMPTY` is 1, the read transfer has completed.

sentences.heading: Programmer's Guide > Controller Module Operations > Reading `n` bytes from a device:
sentences.text: - Retrieve the data from the FIFO by reading `RDATA` `n` times.
